technicalApproach: Explicit durable per-fact exclusion gate. Accepted resume facts plus explicit preferences only. Excluded facts contribute zero; reparse creates reviewable proposals without silently clearing candidate intent. Restoration explicit/reversible; provenance visible; explicit user years wins; no LLM reintroduction.

Approved scope, not completed code. Freeze candidate/profile and accepted/excluded fact snapshots for deterministic matching. Define normalized fact identity and provenance mapping before implementation; a new parse revision never implies consent.
testStrategy: Plan rejected skill/title, repeated search, changed resume revision, normalization-equivalent facts, explicit restore, foreign-owner denial and deterministic-score provenance assertions. Reparse preserves suppression until explicit candidate restoration.

authority: Editorial planning supplement only. Identity, workflow, dependencies, release assignment and source acceptance criteria remain owned by backlog.json. Design mappings remain owned by design/DESIGN-INDEX.json and design-ticket-coverage.json. Generated catalogs and documents are read-only projections.

engineeringEpics.title: Engineering delivery and repository state integrity
Deterministic discovery, matching and owner-scoped data

productInvariants: Candidate owns profile, resume, saved jobs and application decisions. Opening an external application destination never marks Applied.
Do not fabricate ATS/interview/offer/rejection events, unknown data, analytics or verification claims.
Matching remains deterministic; AI cannot silently replace scores, ranking or exclusions.
No autonomous auto-apply, credential/cookie/session theft, CAPTCHA bypass or provider terms/rate-limit bypass.
HOLD/FUTURE features and unapproved provider capabilities stay disabled; design approval is not activation authority.
No new service, technology, schema or endpoint is prescribed merely to reproduce a screenshot.
security: Actor and ownership: authenticated session derives owner; client IDs never choose ownership. Test foreign-owner denial without object-existence disclosure.
Mutations require authoritative validation, same-origin CSRF protection and domain-specific concurrency/idempotency constraints.
Candidate profile/resume/application notes are private; keep raw data, cookies, OAuth/provider tokens, secrets and configuration out of logs, exports, screenshots and evidence.
Admin/recruiter roles require explicit RBAC and consent-scoped projections. No generic database console or unrestricted raw-resume endpoint.
Retention, erasure and audit details must follow the approved domain contract; no undocumented new retention period.
Exercise malformed input, unauthorized actor, stale revision, disabled capability, duplicate request and provider failure where the feature touches those boundaries.
definitionOfDone: Each acceptance criterion has named executable assertions or a dated manual procedure and expected result.
Required unit/integration/contract/browser/accessibility/privacy checks pass for current content under Node >=24; no skips/retries conceal failure.
Documentation and contract agree with implementation; historical evidence is not presented as a new run.
Independent current-content review resolves specification/implementation findings before promotion.
Manual/provider/live gates remain explicit and unexecuted until observed; PROD requires exact reviewed deployed revision acceptance.
Rollback/recovery plan preserves data and encryption material; no irreversible shipping action is authorized by completing a specification.

accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA target: semantic headings/landmarks, accessible names, labels/instructions and associated validation errors.
Keyboard-only navigation with visible focus, logical order, Escape/focus trap/restoration for dialogs, and status/error announcements for async operations.
Non-color status indicators, contrast review, reduced motion and zoom/reflow; NVDA/VoiceOver judgment remains future HUMAN VALIDATION.
responsive: Verify 320, 390, 768, 1024 and 1440px; ordinary content does not cause horizontal overflow; tables have deliberate narrow-screen behavior.
Use mapped approved reference geometry; touch targets and long localized text remain usable; do not invent unsupported mobile designs.
publicSeo: For public/indexable pages: truthful semantic title/description, canonical URL, robots, Open Graph, sitemap and valid structured data where supported.
No private data, fake user counts, fabricated customer claims or future features advertised as active.

approach: Use the canonical root workspace and existing modules; inspect callers and tests before changing a contract.
nonFunctional: Preserve bounded input, deterministic behavior, cancellation/retry semantics and current performance regression thresholds where applicable; do not claim a production SLO.
default.persistence: Preserve owner-scoped PostgreSQL constraints, revisions and append-only migrations; no new database change is inferred from this spec.
default.api: Use registered Fastify routes and the single same-origin client; new operations need reviewed schemas and negative authorization contracts.
observability: Correlate safe request/command/execution identifiers; record failure categories and health without sensitive payloads.
failureModes: Invalid input, concurrency conflict, unavailable dependency, disabled capability and cancellation where applicable.
default.recovery: Restore the prior reviewed code/configuration; preserve stored data and validate migrations separately. Host execution is a later authorized step.

review.reason: The real read-only independent reviewer resumed after the initial usage-limit failure, delivered findings and independently verified the mechanical corrections, including source projection validation, cross-cutting UI scope, honest AC metrics, exact-ID sequencing and CS-25 owner deferral. No unresolved mechanical defect remained among the reviewed fixes. Exact AC bindings, ticket-specific requirements/contracts, design gaps and release decisions remain incomplete. Whole-phase disposition is REVISE, not approval.

CS-46-AC2.preconditions: Future exclusion contract implemented; isolated database migrated; candidate A and candidate B each have synthetic resume and preferences.
CS-46-AC2.setup: A has resume-derived skill 'TypeScript' and title 'Engineer'; neither is in explicit preferences. A declines both, then performs two searches and reparses a changed resume with equivalent normalized facts. B retains accepted facts.
CS-46-AC2.procedure: Read A's matching context and frozen match evidence after rejection, repeated search and reparse; explicitly restore one fact and search again. Attempt to mutate A's exclusions using B's session.
CS-46-AC2.assertion: Rejected normalized facts contribute zero through all three stages; reparse proposes review without clearing exclusions. Explicit restoration returns only the restored fact. B cannot change A's exclusion state; B's accepted facts remain unaffected. Frozen evidence differentiates accepted/profile/excluded provenance.
CS-46-AC2.expectedResult: Candidate intent persists across searches and changed parse revisions with ownership isolation; restoration is explicit and independently scoped.
CS-46-AC2.testName: persists declined resume facts across searches and reparsing until explicit restoration
CS-46-AC2.fixtures: Synthetic owners A/B, two resume parse revisions, normalized-equivalent skills/titles, fixed job snapshot and scoring clock; no production resumes.
CS-46-AC2.negativeCase: Stale or foreign-owner mutation leaves exclusions unchanged; a new parse revision cannot implicitly restore facts; profile-entered years retains precedence over parsed years.
CS-46-AC2.evidenceArtifact: Future exact-content integration run with named test, Node version, database version, exit code and nonzero pass count; sanitized assertions only.
CS-46-AC2.reviewer: Matching domain reviewer, Security reviewer and QA

CS-40.section: CS-40 / CS-88 — admin authorization and admin UX
CS-40.decision: Dedicated privileged Admin Control Plane with server-enforced RBAC, least privilege, seven approved roles and no arbitrary database editor or secret-bearing UI.
CS-40.remainingGate: Exact permission/projection contracts and independent security/design review. Approval does not prove implementation or authorize unrestricted mutations.

CS-44.decision: No second bespoke email-token recovery system. Carry non-enumeration, expiry, single-use, replay rejection and abuse controls into Cognito; preserve authenticated password change/operator recovery until release.
CS-44.remainingGate: Sender identity/domain evidence and security review; historical registration-disabled AC is the pre-Cognito safety boundary, not a ban on approved Cognito signup.

CS-46.decision: Explicit durable per-fact exclusion gate. Accepted resume facts plus explicit preferences only. Excluded facts contribute zero; reparse creates reviewable proposals without silently clearing candidate intent. Restoration explicit/reversible; provenance visible; explicit user years wins; no LLM reintroduction.
CS-46.remainingGate: Implementation/data contract and tests remain unproven. Historical AC2 'until re-parsed' is a lower bound, not permission to clear exclusions on reparse; later owner direction governs.

CS-88.section: CS-40 / CS-88 — admin authorization and admin UX
CS-88.decision: Admin Control Plane scope approved; imported Design System is visual authority; real redacted API data or honest unavailable states only.
CS-88.remainingGate: Exact per-screen responsive mappings, RBAC/API contracts and actual named independent reviews. Functional approval is not proof every screen is designed.

CS-89.decision: Assistive preparation/explanation approved but production default-OFF; never control deterministic ranking, authorization, identity, verification or application state.
CS-89.remainingGate: Runtime secret, current provider-catalog free-model proof, budget/kill switch, exact-SHA live verification and rollback remain required; no activation in this phase.

CS-90.decision: ap-south-1; verified normalized case-insensitive email; phone optional contact with phone OTP later; server provider exchange into opaque CareerScope session; auth.careerscope.tech after DNS/TLS; controlled owner linking without hash export; flagged canary with Argon2 rollback.
CS-90.remainingGate: Specific pool settings, threat/retention review and actual DNS/TLS/provider evidence remain unproven. Region/identifier no longer require a fresh decision.

CS-91.decision: Initial email signup/OTP, not mobile OTP expansion; provider tokens stay server-side, never browser-persisted; preserve opaque application sessions and canary rollback.
CS-91.remainingGate: Exact OTP/session contracts, negative tests and real Cognito acceptance; phone OTP remains later capability.

CS-92.decision: Verified CareerScope domain identity is sender target; actual From/Reply-To and SES access are operational/DNS evidence, not assumptions.
CS-92.remainingGate: Addresses, supported locales and template visual acceptance are not specified here. DNS/bounce/deliverability and real-message verification remain external acceptance.

CS-93.decision: Email-first Cognito exchange into opaque application sessions; no browser provider-token persistence; preserve workspace reachability and rollback.
CS-93.remainingGate: Exact signup/OTP/error/outage/recovery design states and keyboard/browser review plus real session-exchange proof.

CS-94.decision: Flagged canary with Argon2/session rollback until disposable E2E, monitoring and owner continuity are proven.
CS-94.remainingGate: Protected exact-SHA deployment and redacted live evidence; owner acceptance only after actual evidence; no deployment now.

CS-25.decision: Historical owner deferral is retained as registry provenance, not blanket future release authorization. Current single-owner baseline may use verified local backups; encrypted off-host protection, retention, restored verification, monitoring and RPO/RTO are required before materially multi-user/public/recruiter rollout.
CS-25.remainingGate: Actual scheduled dump, failure alert and restore proof remain unproven by this specification. No local-only backup is disaster recovery; release reviewer must enforce the newer multi-user boundary even though frozen delivery metadata records DEFERRED_BY_OWNER.
